full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J.: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.3.94 passed by the Addl. District Jud Court, Comilla in Misc. Case No. 50 of 1 rejecting the appellant's application under Section-263 of the Succession Act, 1925 praying for revocation of the probate earlier granted by the Court. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that testator Debendra Kumar Chakraborty executed on 17.4.67 a will (registered) in favour of his wife Raj Luxmi Debi. Subsequently, Debendra Kumar Chakra-borty died on 29.9.68 at his native village in Comilla. Thereafter Raj Luxmi Debi filed a probate suit before the Subordinate Judge and District Delegate Comilla, being Probate Suit No. 463 of 1979 (testamentary suit) praying probate of the will executed by Debendra Kumar Chakraborty and subsequently obtained an order of probate in her favour. 

 3. The petitioner thereafter filed a case before the District Judge, Comilla, under Section-263 of the Succession Act, 1925 being Misc. Case No. 50 of 1989, praying for revocation of the probate granted to legatee Raj Luxmi Debi alleging inter alia that testator Debendra Kumar Chakraborty did not execute any will in favour of his wife Raj Luxmi Debi and the alleged will is forged and fabricated. It was contended that the Raj Luxmi Debi by practising fraud upon the Court obtained probate in Misc. Case No. 463 of 1979 on misrepresentation of facts, seriously affecting the interest of the Government. It has been contended that some of the co-sharers of the property involved in the case migrated to India before 1965 and permanently settled there as a result of which their property became vested property by operation of law and, consequently serious prejudice has been caused to the petitioner, which necessitated the filing of the case for revocation of .the probate granted to Raj Luxmi Debi. 

 4. The learned 'Addl. District Judge, Comilla who heard Misc. Case No. 50 of 1989, has been pleased by the impugned judgment and order dated 27.3.84 to dismiss the case oili contest on the finding that the petitioner has no locus standi to challenge the probate granted to Raj Luxmi Debi. 

 6. Mr. Fazlul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the learned District Judge was wrong in dismissing the case without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 7. Mr. H. N. Nondy, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents on the other hand submits that the petitioner being a stranger to the will and not claiming through the testator the learned Addl. District Judge was perfectly justified in dismissing Misc. Case No. 50 of 1989 on proper consideration of the facts of the case and the law bearing on the subject and as such there is no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. 

 10. In this case there is no dispute to the fact that testator Debendra Kumar Chakra-borty died leaving behind his wife Raj Luxmi Debi as his only legatee. Raj Luxmi Debi is admittedly a citizen of Bangladesh. So, by no stretch of immigration the property of Raj Luxmi Debi can be claimed to be vested property. There is no dispute to the fact that the appellant does not claim interest in the suit property through testator Debendra Kumar Chakraborti but it lays its claim through some outsiders alleged to have migrated to India before 1965, as a result of which their property allegedly became vested property by operation of law. The claim of the petitioner that some portion of the suit property belonging to some of the co-sharers thereto is vested property cannot be gone into and decided in a probate proceeding. Moreover, except merely laying a verbal claim that a portion of the suit property is a vested property by operation of law, the petitioner has placed nothing on record to substantiate that claim. The settled law on this point is that a mere claim by the Government that a certain property is a vested property has no sanctity in the eye of law, unless that claim is proved by the Government by cogent legal evidence. The onus of the strict proof of such a claim lies squarely on 'the Government authority. 

 12. We get instant support of our view in the case reported in 21 D.LR 331, 40 D.L.R. 120 33 D.L.R. (AD) and 284. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record we are satisfied that the learned Addl. District Judge rightly dismissed the appellant's case for revocation of the probate. The efforts made by the petitioner are found to be totally misconceived exercises. We, therefore, find no merit in the appeal and it fails necessarily. 

 13. In the result, the appeal is dismissed on contest without any order as to costs and the Mpugned judgment and order dated 27.9.94 passed by the learned Addl. District Judge. Comilla in Misc. Case No. 50 of 1989 dismissing the case on contest are affirmed.
